title: Senior's toolkit: vim with the shell, and VS Code
summary: Macros, project-wide search and replace, shell filters, and the VS Code keys and remote features most teams work in every day.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: vim with the shell, and VS Code
steps.body: vim gets its real power from the shell and from editing many files at once. Most teams also live in VS Code, so its handful of power keys belongs on the same card.

toolkit.what: Record a macro into register `a`, replay it, replay the last one. Turns a fiddly edit on one line into the same edit on 200 lines.
flags: play it 50 times (it stops at the first failure)
toolkit.when: start the macro with a motion like `0` and end with `j`, so it repeats cleanly

toolkit.what: Search a whole project and put every hit in the quickfix list, then open it. Enter on a line jumps to that file and line.
flags: the same with an external tool, e.g. `set grepprg=rg\ --vimgrep`

toolkit.what: Run a substitution on every quickfix hit and save each file. A project-wide rename with a list you checked first.
flags: run once per file in the list
write the file only if it changed

toolkit.what: Filter the buffer through a shell command and replace it with the output. Pretty-print JSON, sort lines, format anything.
flags: insert a command's output below the cursor, e.g. `:r !date -u`

toolkit.what: List open buffers, switch by part of the name, split the window. Keep a config and its log side by side.
flags: switch to the buffer whose name contains `part` (Tab completes)
diff two files side by side

toolkit.what: VS Code: the command palette (every command by name), quick open a file by fuzzy name, go to a symbol in the current file. On macOS use Cmd for Ctrl.
flags: open file by name; type `:42` to go to a line

toolkit.what: VS Code: add the next match to a multi-cursor, add a cursor anywhere, rename a symbol everywhere through the language server, go to definition.
flags: select the next occurrence (Ctrl+Shift+L: all of them)
rename symbol: safe across files, unlike text replace
go to definition / find all references

toolkit.what: VS Code runs its server on a remote machine or inside a container, so search, terminals, debugging and extensions work there as if local.
flags: from a terminal inside the remote, opens that folder
toolkit.when: debugging on a test VM, or giving the whole team the same toolchain

steps.prompt: Match each command to the job it does.
pairs: pretty-print the JSON in the buffer
show the list of search hits
insert a command's output into the file
rename a symbol across the project
open a file by typing part of its name

steps.prompt: Rename `OldClient` to `NewClient` in every C# file of the project from inside vim, checking the hits before you change anything.
lines: Read the list and check every hit

steps.prompt: An API returns a 4 KB response on one line and you pasted it into vim to find a field. What makes it readable fastest?
options: Copy it into a website that formats JSON
steps.explain: `jq .` parses and indents the JSON, and an error from jq also tells you it is not valid JSON. Splitting on commas breaks strings that contain commas, and pasting a real response into a website can leak tokens or customer data.

steps.prompt: A bug only happens on the test VM, behind a bastion host. You want breakpoints and the variables window, not `printf`. What is the usual setup?
options: VS Code Remote-SSH to the VM (with `ProxyJump` in `~/.ssh/config`), then F9 and F5 there
Copy the VM's disk to your laptop
Edit on the VM with nano and add log lines
Open the VM's files over a network share in Notepad
steps.explain: Remote-SSH runs the editor's server on the VM, so the debugger, terminal and search run where the bug is. `ProxyJump` in your SSH config takes care of the bastion.

items: Rename a C# method called from 30 files
Change `http://` to `https://` in a YAML file
Rename a property that is also a common word in comments
Replace a typo in Markdown docs
Rename a TypeScript interface used across packages

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: In vim, reach for the shell (`:%!`, `:r !`) and the quickfix list whenever a change spans many lines or files. In VS Code, learn the palette and `F2` first: renaming through the language server is safer than any regex, and Remote-SSH means you can debug where the problem lives.
